The Waldheim Alpine Spa sits inside Cradle Mountain Lodge on the edge of the Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area, beside the Pencil Pine River and surrounded by ancient forest. It’s a treatment spa first, facials, body rituals, a considered menu of native-ingredient treatments, but its centrepiece is the Sanctuary: a private circuit of hot tub, cool plunge pool, sauna and steam room enclosed by King Billy pines.

The Sanctuary is a private circuit of hot tub, cool plunge pool, sauna and steam room enclosed by King Billy pines, one of the more unusual settings for a hot-cold session in Australia.

The treatment list leans into Australian native botanicals. There’s a foot bathing ceremony using melaleuca flower and strawberry gum, a full-body ritual built around lime caviar and Kakadu plum, and a range of facials, body wraps and signature rituals. All treatments use the Waterlily artisanal spa collection. It’s a well-considered menu for a remote mountain location.

The spa hasn’t published pricing publicly, so ring them on (03) 6492 2133 before you plan around a particular budget. Hours are 9am to 5pm daily.

The spa rates 4.4 out of 5 across 82 Google reviews, and individual staff members are named and praised with unusual specificity in what people mention, a sign of a small team doing the personal side of things well.

Individual staff members are named and praised with unusual specificity in reviews, a sign of a small team doing the personal side of things well.

You don’t need to be a lodge guest to book, day visitors are taken. That said, advance bookings are strongly recommended. Cradle Mountain Road is a long drive from anywhere, and arriving without a confirmed booking risks a wasted trip. The Sanctuary in particular, being private, is likely to fill on busier days. Book before you make the drive.

FAQ

What's included in the Sanctuary session?
The Sanctuary is a private circuit with a hot tub, cool plunge pool, sauna and steam room, set in a secluded area surrounded by King Billy pines. Reviews suggest sessions run around an hour, though the spa's materials don't specify a fixed duration, worth confirming when you book.
Do I need to be staying at Cradle Mountain Lodge to use the spa?
No, the spa takes bookings from day visitors, not just lodge guests. Advance bookings are highly recommended, especially in peak season.
What treatments are on offer beyond the Sanctuary?
The treatment menu includes a foot bathing ceremony using native melaleuca flower and strawberry gum, a full-body ritual with lime caviar and Kakadu plum, performance facials, body wraps, and signature rituals. Products are from the Waterlily artisanal spa collection.
Is pricing available in advance?
No pricing information is publicly listed, contact the spa directly on (03) 6492 2133 for current rates.
Do I need to book ahead?
Yes, advance bookings are highly recommended. Given the remote location and the Sanctuary's private format, turning up without a reservation is a risk not worth taking.

4038 Cradle Mountain Rd, Cradle Mountain TAS 7306

Part of Cradle Mountain Lodge, day spa visitors can book treatments or the Sanctuary session without being a lodge guest.
